parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
Listeners to this programme will know that we're very keen to foster links within communities, and we think we've hit on a winning idea. I'm going to tell you about a scheme which has been set up as part of our Communities in Action programme for those who'd like to be put in touch with people from different countries and cultures. As the name Connections suggests, we're hoping that the scheme will introduce people who live in this country who act as hosts to people who've recently arrived here to study or to work for a limited period of time, who will be their guests.

Now, if you've got a spare room in your house or flat, you might like to be able to have someone stay for a weekend. I should point out that no money is involved, as all our hosts are unpaid, but you should not have too much extra expense other than one more person joining you at mealtimes. In the course of their studies or work in this country, some people rarely get the opportunity to socialise.

There may be language problems or feelings of shyness, which mean that whatever their age, people can become quite lonely or isolated. If you're prepared to invite someone into your home, you can rely on Connections for a personal introduction, and the timing of the invitation will be to suit you. As I said, the stay is always over a weekend for two or three nights and, as the host, the arrangements you make for your visitor will depend on your other commitments.

If you're listening to this programme and you would like to take advantage of what Connections can offer a guest, then what I'm going on to say will apply to you. So, what will you, the guest, get out of a visit? You'll gain an insight into the customs and way of life of the country you're staying in, and you'll enjoy home-cooked meals and be able to ask questions about things which interest you or perhaps even puzzle you. It's early days, but if a weekend goes well, relationships might develop over time and turn into lasting and genuine friendships.

This would undoubtedly be of advantage to the whole community, as we all become more aware of the ways in which people in different countries live their lives. There's also the possibility that, when you return to your own country, you might one day want to invite your hosts to stay with you.

Right, I hope I've given you enough information on the scheme and what we're setting out to do. I'll now deal with the process for applying, if you'd like to be involved from the point of view of a guest. So have a pencil and some paper ready to jot down what you need to do.

Connections is broken up into various small sections which will deal with your application through the different stages. To begin with, we ask you to make a phone call to our vetting people. We need to know some basic information about you, like how long you're intending to be in this country.

The minimum time limit is three months. Whether you're working or studying, we require a reference, which must be from the person in authority who you're working with or studying under. This will be used for an identity check.

Once that's been sent to the authorities and approved, we'll email you an application form which you can download. You should complete this and return it with two recent passport-sized photographs of yourself. One photo will be held in our records and the other will be sent to your host family prior to your first weekend visit.

Our centre manager will get back to you within a week of receiving your form to let you know that we have it, and if we think there's a suitable match on our files, someone from our interview team will contact you for a face-to-face meeting with a member of staff. At that point, you should have some idea of weekend dates when you're free, which we can put to the host family. However, decisions are not made at the meeting, but you can expect to hear the result from us in a couple of days.

analyses.content: To begin with, we ask you to make a phone call to our vetting people. We need to know some basic information about you, like how long you're intending to be in this country.
如果你只盯着“application”去听，可能会因为没听清具体部门而漏掉vetting这个关键限定词。
录音里直接说给“vetting people”打电话，对应选项H（审查部门）。
录音说推荐信将被用于“identity check”，也就是确认你的身份，对应选项C。
Whether you're working or studying, we require a reference, which must be from the person in authority who you're working with or studying under. This will be used for an identity check.
你可能听到“working or studying”就想选E（法律地位），但这只是开推荐信的要求，而不是提供推荐信的核心目的。
One photo will be held in our records and the other will be sent to your host family prior to your first weekend visit.
填空时要分清两张照片的去向，如果你听到“sent to your host family”就选错了。
原文明确说其中一张照片会“held in our records”（保存在记录中），对应选项F。
Our centre manager will get back to you within a week of receiving your form to let you know that we have it...
你可能听到“a week”（七天）后就想选B或D，但录音明确说这通电话只是为了让你知道他们收到了表，还没到面试或做决定。
录音提到经理会联系你并告知“we have it”（我们收到了申请表），这在流程中属于确认收到的“告知/回执”，对应选项A。
...if we think there's a suitable match on our files, someone from our interview team will contact you for a face-to-face meeting with a member of staff.
这里容易跟第18题搞混，记住18题是收表回执，19题才是真正和工作人员（staff member）见面。
原文提到会联系你进行一个“face-to-face meeting”，这对应了选项D（面试）。
However, decisions are not made at the meeting, but you can expect to hear the result from us in a couple of days.
你可能在面试环节就想听到结果，但原文提醒“decisions are not made at the meeting”，所以一定要往后听最后的处理结果。
录音最后说在几天内你会听到“the result”，即最终结果或决定，对应选项B。
